subject: Hosted eval: staging endpoints and throttling plan
thread_text:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted eval: staging endpoints and throttling plan

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

- Recap: You liked the low-latency streaming and the prefix caching idea for user completions. The main downstream decision is whether to run the pilot on Hosted API (fastest to get started) or request Dedicated capacity (if predictable sustained throughput is required).
- Ask: To recommend an onramp plan we need a short traffic sample: expected concurrent requests, avg tokens per request, and spikes (peak TPS) during business hours. See the sample table below you can paste into a reply.

Suggested short form traffic sample:
- Primary endpoint: /v1/generate (chat-style)
- Avg requests/sec (baseline): ___
- Peak requests/sec (burst/minute): ___
- Avg tokens/request: ___
- Percent of heavy prompts (>512 tokens): ___

Proposed pilot path (Hosted-first):
1) Provide traffic sample -> we provision a staging project and ephemeral staging endpoints.
2) You validate latency and correctness with a small corpus (we recommend 1k representative calls).
3) If sustained load looks high we can propose a Dedicated pool estimate and a migration plan.

Immediate next steps I can own: create staging endpoints, load a short MAP that lists acceptance criteria, and put together the throttling matrix. Can you confirm the traffic sample by EOD Monday?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.ai]

---

From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Nov 2027 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: staging endpoints and throttling plan

Jonas —

Thanks for the concise plan. We are comfortable starting on Hosted for the pilot but need to validate that throttling won't bust our UX during peak hours. Preliminary numbers from our engineering lead:
- Baseline avg requests/sec: 6
- Peak bursts: 45 req/sec (sustained ~2m once/day during batch ingest)
- Avg tokens/request: 280
- Heavy prompts (>512 tokens): ~5%

Security note: we have to confirm network policy and a SOC‑2 scoping question. Priya will follow up on that list.

Can you provision staging endpoints scoped to slow bursts (e.g., 50 req/s) so we can run a load test? Also please include a throttling matrix (per-endpoint rate limit and backoff guidance).

Thanks,
Sanjay Mehta
CTO, FinLytics
[sanjay@finlytics.com]

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: staging endpoints and throttling plan

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

I've created a staging project under your account name (FinLytics-staging). Staging endpoints and a recommended throttling matrix are attached as a CSV. High-level notes:

- Staging endpoints:
  - https://staging.redwood.ai/finlytics/generate (default chat endpoint)
  - https://staging.redwood.ai/finlytics/embeddings
  - https://staging.redwood.ai/finlytics/re-rank
- Default throttling (suggested for pilot on Hosted):
  - generate: 60 req/s per API key, with a soft 5xx backoff of 2s and exponential backoff thereafter.
  - embeddings: 30 req/s per API key.
  - re-rank: 20 req/s per API key.
- Rationale: Your peak burst of ~45 req/s for generate fits within 60 req/s per API key. If you plan to do many concurrent users, we can provide a tokenized partitioning strategy (multiple API keys / worker pools) to distribute load.

Attached: MAP-FinLytics-v1.pdf (mutual action plan) and staging-endpoints-matrix.csv (throttles).

If you want, we can temporarily raise the staging limit to 100 req/s for a one-hour load test — let me know when you want the window.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[laura.bennett@redwood.ai]

Attachment stubs:
[Attachment: MAP-FinLytics-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 384KB)]
[Attachment: staging-endpoints-matrix.csv (text/csv, 8KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: staging endpoints and throttling plan

Sanjay —

Quick technical clarifications from infra/product:
- Model variants: We'll provision a single model variant for pilot (gpt-rlm-medium) that is latency-optimized. If you require a lower-cost quantized variant we can include that in a later step.
- KV/prefix caching: For your chat flows we should enable prefix caching; it will reduce per-token cost ~12% on average.
- SLA & trial credits: For a 30-day pilot we can offer $6k in trial credits and a pilot addendum SLA (non-binding) — I'll share a DocuSign link once you sign the MAP.

DocuSign (pilot addendum): https://docusign.example.com/r/AA987654321

I'll stand by to temporarily raise staging throttles to 100 req/s for your one-hour test if you confirm a window (and we will capture telemetry to validate latency SLOs).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
VP, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
[aditya.rao@redwood.ai]

Perfect — this is exactly what we needed. Next steps from FinLytics:
1) Priya will send the SOC-2 scoping answers by tomorrow noon.
2) We will run a 1-hour load test on Wed, Dec 1 at 14:00 PST; please enable the 100 req/s staging window for 14:00–15:00 PST.
3) I'll review the MAP and sign the pilot addendum (DocuSign) if the load test looks good.

Jonas, please confirm the staging window and that telemetry will be available for the load-test session.

—Sanjay
